clue.text: Straight and flat

definitions.meaning: being straight is being honest and above board
flat ground has no slope, being perfectly horizontal

explanation.surface: A description of something both straight and flat, like a level table top.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both honest (fair dealing) and horizontal (no tilt), matching each sense in turn.

clue.text: Shorty, for instance, exploding with anger

indicators.note: exploding blows the letters of the phrase apart so they land in a new order

explanation.surface: A short-tempered man flies into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shorty' looks like a person's nickname; it is a short nightdress. 'exploding' rearranges WITH ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A shorty is a brief nightdress, one example of clothes worn to bed.

clue.text: House reflected on a noisy commotion

parts.note: the same abbreviation for house again, now in its mirror image

indicators.note: reflected suggests a mirror image, so the house abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: the same abbreviation for house again, now in its mirror image

explanation.surface: A house's reflection appears amid a noisy row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns the house abbreviation into its mirror image, and 'on' simply places the pieces one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is a fuss or uproar, a synonym for a noisy commotion.

clue.text: Unusually big turtle — he's very untidy

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of the two words come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: An unusually large turtle turns out to be a slob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges BIG TURTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who drops rubbish in public places is a classic untidy person.

clue.text: A small amount injected into plant — it protects against disease

indicators.note: injected into means one piece is placed inside another, as a syringe enters the body

parts.note: a vine is a climbing plant
CC, a cubic centimetre, is a small measured quantity

explanation.surface: A gardener injects a little medicine into a plant to guard it from disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injected into' suits the medical surface: the small dose goes into the plant. CC is a cubic centimetre.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaccine primes the immune system so the body resists infection.

clue.text: Stay in bed till late, right? About one

indicators.note: About here means wrapped around, so the legal right surrounds the numeral

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone asks for confirmation that they may sleep late until about one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right?' reads as a tag question, but it is LIEN, a legal right; 'About' puts it round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-in is a morning spent in bed beyond the usual rising hour.

clue.text: Kick from a horse

definitions.meaning: in football and rugby, to kick an opponent's shins is to ... them
a horse for ordinary riding, often hired out

explanation.surface: A horse lashes out with a kick.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: hacking is kicking a player, and a riding horse is called a hack.

clue.text: Breathe in, out… in sleep

indicators.note: out means the letters are disordered, put out of their usual places

explanation.surface: Breathing instructions given while drifting off to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges BREATHE IN; the second 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To hibernate is to pass the winter in a deep sleep-like state, as bears do.

clue.text: Clubs are inclined to be spotless

parts.note: C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs
to lean is to be inclined or tilted

explanation.surface: Golf clubs are expected to be kept spotless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no spots or stains is unsoiled, the same idea as spotless.

clue.text: One who's uncertain about it lied — answer rejected

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
taken as written
a Lied is a German art song

explanation.surface: A doubter tells a lie about something, and their answer is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lied' looks like the past tense of lie; it is the German for song. 'rejected' turns C+IT+SONG+A into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic holds that whether God exists cannot be known, so is uncertain on the question.

clue.text: Device revealed by turning pound note repeatedly around

indicators.note: turning means the assembled letters are read backwards
around means the pair of notes surrounds the weight abbreviation
repeatedly means the note is used twice over

parts.note: ME (also MI) is the third note of the sol-fa scale
LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: A design emerges when a banknote is spun round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' tempts as money (L); here it is the weight abbreviation. 'repeatedly' doubles the note, 'around' wraps it round the weight, and 'turning' reverses the result.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a device is a badge or symbol, which is what an emblem is.

clue.text: The way airmen choose ultimately to attack?

parts.note: ST, for street, is a common abbreviation for a way
the RAF is the Royal Air Force, Britain's airmen

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A question about how air force crews decide to launch an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF is Britain's air force.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack ground targets with fire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: No rating could be so dense

indicators.note: could be invites the letters to be rearranged into what they might become

explanation.surface: A remark that only a slow-witted person would rate something as nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges NO RATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense, used of a person, means slow to understand or lacking knowledge.

clue.text: Man with old record coming in second

parts.note: a man is referred to as he
an LP, a long-playing vinyl album, is an old type of record

explanation.surface: A man arrives with a vintage album and finishes runner-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' here is the verb, to back up or assist.
explanation.definitionFit: To second someone is to support or assist them, as in seconding a motion.

clue.text: Book by scholar included in collection

indicators.note: included in means these pieces go inside the collection

parts.note: a pack is a collection, as of cards
per means by, as in per post
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar

explanation.surface: A book written by an academic is part of a series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' places 'by' and 'scholar' inside the collection; 'Book' at the front is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperback is a book with soft card covers.

clue.text: Tame rat we trained, or mole

parts.note: to break a horse is to tame it

indicators.note: trained suggests reshaping, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A tamed rat, or perhaps a mole, has been trained by us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' looks like the animal beside 'rat'; it is a harbour pier. 'trained' rearranges RAT WE into WATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a stone pier or sea wall shielding a harbour from waves.

clue.text: Edging within earshot, checks sound

indicators.note: within earshot says the word is heard rather than read, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: to curb is to check or restrain
a tone is a sound

explanation.surface: Someone within hearing distance keeps an eye on the noise.
explanation.walkthrough: A kerb is the British spelling of the stone edge of a pavement (US curb).
explanation.definitionFit: Kerbstones form the raised border along a road, an edging for the pavement.

clue.text: Briefbook Green left unfinished

parts.note: EPH is the abbreviation for Ephesians, a book of the Bible

indicators.note: left unfinished means the colour word loses its last letter

parts.note: emerald is a bright green

explanation.surface: A short book called Green is abandoned before its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left unfinished' drops the D from EMERALD.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral means lasting a very short time, so brief.

clue.text: One helps with growing support — a gun, and soldiers

parts.note: a prop is a support
gat is slang for a gun
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A gardener's helper is armed and backed by troops.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is a crossword staple for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A propagator is a heated tray or box where seedlings are raised, so it aids plant growth.

clue.text: Lad of considerable stature and large chest

definitions.meaning: a ... is a lad of great height
a tall chest of drawers, often in two stacked parts

explanation.surface: A tall youth beside a big piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a lofty youngster; as one it is a high chest of drawers.

clue.text: Some employee chosen to return call

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A worker is picked to ring a client back.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound coming back, a call returned off a surface.

clue.text: Call out, including name of office worker

indicators.note: including means the rearranged letters wrap around the name
out signals that the letters of the word before are disordered

parts.note: Eric is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone shouts out a name in a typing pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call out' reads as shouting, but 'out' scrambles the letters of Call, and 'including' wraps them round the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Clerical describes the work of a clerk, the paperwork of an office.

clue.text: "It's like a camel"., priest said

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: A priest remarks that something resembles a camel.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American llama is related to the camel and looks rather like a small humpless one.

clue.text: One may be seen standing up for a publication

definitions.text: One may be seen standing up
definitions.meaning: a stand-up entertainer performs on their feet telling jokes

explanation.surface: Someone standing up to promote a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up comedian is a comic, and a cartoon magazine is also a comic.

clue.text: Obsequious NCO attached to force

parts.note: SM, sergeant major, is a non-commissioned officer
an army is a military force

explanation.surface: A fawning sergeant is posted to a military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy means oily and ingratiating, the manner of a fawning, obsequious person.

clue.text: A jolly journalist all set to go off

parts.note: a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
ED, an editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A cheerful reporter is ready to set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective; it is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb that is armed is primed and ready to explode.

clue.text: Mixedincendiary materials finally burn a tree

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word after it

parts.note: a palm is a tree

explanation.surface: Fire-starting compounds are used at the end to torch a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm is a jellied blend of petrol and thickener used in fire bombs.

clue.text: Lingerie for boobs

definitions.meaning: baggy knickers once worn by women

explanation.surface: Underwear chosen for one's bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boobs' tempts as the body part; here it means mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are loose women's knickers, and also embarrassing blunders.

clue.text: He may be found in or on deck

definitions.text: He may be found in or on deck

parts.words: He may be found in or on deck
parts.note: a playing-card picture in a deck of cards, or a sailor on a ship's deck

explanation.surface: A man who turns up in a pack of cards or aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The knave in a deck of cards, and a sailor (jack tar) on board, share this one name.

clue.text: Horse English boys brought back on river

parts.note: the Clyde is the river through Glasgow

indicators.note: brought back means these pieces are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: lads are boys

explanation.surface: English lads are returned home on a Scottish river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses E+LADS to SDALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Clydesdale is a heavy Scottish breed of draught horse.
